title: vdog original recording v1 active-state record
description: Bounded recoverable active-state record at /vdog/v1/clips/<clip_id>/active.json, published and synced before the first payload append (docs/specs/media-format.md section 5). It uses the manifest field rules for the fields it carries and must serialize within 16,384 bytes. While it exists the payload and index use .part names and no valid final manifest may exist.

capture_order.description: Reserved durably in the card catalog before capture; gaps allowed.

firmware_version.description: Opaque version string. Length is bounded only by the whole-record 16,384-byte invariant; the spec assigns no per-field limit.

hardware_revision.description: Acquired hardware revision label. Length is bounded only by the whole-record 16,384-byte invariant.

start_boot_us.description: Monotonic first-frame time for that boot.

device_id.description: 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters provisioned once. The length keywords restate what the pattern already implies in this dialect, so a reader whose regex engine treats $ loosely still refuses an identifier with a stray byte glued to it.

boot_id.description: 32 random lowercase hexadecimal characters per boot; never reveals a MAC address. The length keywords restate what the pattern already implies in this dialect, so a reader whose regex engine treats $ loosely still refuses an identifier with a stray byte glued to it.

clip_id.description: <boot_id>-<sequence> with exactly eight lowercase hexadecimal digits. Equality between the prefix and boot_id is a cross-field invariant. The length keywords restate what the pattern already implies in this dialect, so a reader whose regex engine treats $ loosely still refuses an identifier with a stray byte glued to it.

width.description: Positive; each dimension at most 1600 and it must match the JPEG SOF.

height.description: Positive; each dimension at most 1600 and it must match the JPEG SOF.

nominal_fps.description: Nominal integer rate; actual rate may be lower and comes from timestamps.

jpeg_quality.description: esp32-camera driver quality parameter, not a percentage. The spec assigns no numeric range, so only nonnegativity is required here.

start_utc.description: RFC3339 UTC with millisecond precision and trailing Z, or null when the clock source is unknown. The pairing of null-ness with source is a validator invariant.

uncertainty_ms.description: Required and nonnegative when the clock source is known; null when unknown. media-format.md §2 puts every JSON integer of this format inside the range a conforming reader represents exactly, so an estimate above that ceiling is not an estimate at all.
